answer: PoA attenuates each trust contribution exponentially with age, using a fixed half-life, so reputation must be earned through sustained honest service rather than a burst of endorsements. A new identity—whether named jetty, juniper, or dawn—starts with near-zero eigenvector centrality; without trusted, reciprocal paths from established agents, it cannot inflate its score through sybil-to-sybil links or meet consensus thresholds. This raises the cost of identity churn, though it cannot eliminate collusion.
